in_english.name: Lazarus
in_english.meaning: healer, God's messenger, brought back to life
in_english.long_meaning: Lazarus, a figure in the New Testament, is the third person Jesus raised from the dead (John 11:1-44). His name means 'healer' or 'God's messenger' in Hebrew and 'apostle' or 'sent one' in Greek. Lazarus is often associated with resurrection and the power of faith. In Christian tradition, he is considered a saint and a model of devotion and perseverance. His story has been influential in art and literature throughout history, symbolizing the triumph of life over death.

biblical_reference.note: The story of Lazarus is told in the Gospel of John, chapter 11, verses 1-44.

saint_reference.note: Saint Lazarus of Bethany is a Christian saint and a figure in the New Testament, known for his resurrection by Jesus Christ.

data.cultural_impact: The name Lazarus stands as a powerful symbol of the Christian belief in the power of rebirth and resurrection. The story of Lazarus, being the fourth Gospel account of a miracle in which Jesus raises a man named Lazarus from the dead, has had a lasting impact on Christian tradition and art. Images of Lazarus rising from his tomb, bound in burial shrouds, are a common motif in Christian art and symbolize the promise of eternal life.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Lazarus spiritually signifies new life, renewal, and the hope of resurrection. The story of Lazarus not only speaks to the power of Jesus as the giver of life but also serves as reminder of the belief in life after death. The name Lazarus can be a source of comfort and inspiration to those facing difficult times, reminding us that no matter how lost we may feel, we too can be raised from our figurative tombs and given the gift of new life.
